title: Stable graph recapture and token-atomicity for stream-owned decodes
creator: Aisha Ramesh
description: Problem: We observe intermittent token duplication, dropped tokens, and kernel launch stalls when replaying CUDA Graphs captured across different CUDA streams and device contexts. Symptoms show up on bursty traffic with variable prefix lengths and during warmup when multiple decodes race to capture. Root cause appears to be a combination of: (1) non-idempotent capture sequences when stream ownership changes mid-prefill, (2) inconsistent recording of per-stream event dependencies for KV cache prefill and consumption, and (3) kernel selection heuristics that pick different kernel variants during recapture vs original capture resulting in mismatched replay paths. This ticket implements a robust recapture & fallback strategy that guarantees replay correctness and preserves token-level atomicity across multi-stream decodes. Goals: ensure idempotent graph recapture, maintain deterministic per-token ordering under concurrent captures, and provide safe fallback with limited latency impact when recapture cannot be validated.
acceptance_criteria: No token duplication or loss in 10k synthetic chat sessions with randomized prefix lengths and parallel decodes
Successful graph replay rate >= 99.9% under variable batch sizes and stream handoffs
End-to-end P90 decode latency regression <= 5% compared to non-graph baseline under 95th percentile load
Automated CI test that injects capture-time kernel-variant divergence and verifies fallback path correctness
implementation_notes: Introduce StreamOwnershipGuard: an RAII-style guard that pins capture to a stable logical stream context; captures record a stable stream id token for later validation
Record a signature during capture: (kernel-variant-hash, kv-cache-layout, tensor-dtypes, launch-params). On recapture, validate signature before committing replay
When validation fails, fall back to a deterministic non-graph decode for affected sequence with lightweight telemetry emitted
Add a recapture backoff policy: allow limited automatic recapture attempts with exponential backoff and jitter to avoid thundering recapture storms
Kernel selection change: prefer stable-kernel family for capture (avoid variants that depend on ephemeral heuristics like occupancy estimation) and mark compatibility groups
Ensure CUDA events inserted around KV cache prefill/prefetch regions are recorded and replayed with cross-stream dependency checks
Expose a debug flag RUNTIME_CG_VALIDATE=1 to force signature validation in dev builds and log mismatch diffs for triage
test_plan: 1) Unit tests for signature generation/validation. 2) Deterministic replay integration tests exercising stream handoffs and recapture attempts. 3) Fuzz harness that randomizes prefix lengths, batch sizes, and kernel selection to surface mismatch cases. 4) Canary rollout on dedicated staging with synthetic load generator measuring token correctness and latency. 5) Add CI gating job that runs nightly long-run stability workload (2 hours) and asserts no token anomalies.
benchmarks: Current graph-enabled P50/P90 (unstable capture): 18ms / 55ms with 0.6% token anomalies observed in stress run
Post-change target P50/P90: 20ms / 58ms with <=0.1% token anomalies and >99.9% replay success
risk: Medium. Changes increase capture-time metadata and validation cost; improper fallback could increase tail latency. Must validate compatibility matrix across kernel families and hardware generations (A100, H100).
rollout_plan: - Merge behind feature flag: runtime.graph_recapture_validation=false by default. - Run canary on dedicated pool for internal customers only. - Monitor token-level diffs and graph-replay success metric. - Gradually enable validation for 10%/50%/100% of traffic. - If regressions observed, disable and collect artifacts for triage.
monitoring: log: cg_signature_mismatch -> include capture_signature and recapture_signature (hashed)

notes: Design trade-off: signing every capture adds a ~0.5ms overhead on capture path; acceptable given correctness guarantees for high-tier customers
Open question: Should we persist capture signatures on disk to enable cross-process validation after restarts? Tentative NO for 1.22 due to rollback complexity
